decision.detail: I let the evening go by on the empty depot bench. The station line hums its open tone behind me, red light steady, but I don't turn. The coach sits in the lot out the window, windows dark, already loaded, already waiting. I can smell the diesel and the cold iron of the tracks. My hands are in my lap. I count the seconds the way I count raindrops on a window in a live broadcast, just keeping the count, just keeping the body still. I don't pick up the phone. I don't go to the ballroom. I don't go to the Rialto. I sit. The depot is empty and the bench is cold through my jacket and the tracks are black and the light in the lot is the only light and I stay in it until I can't feel my fingers anymore and then I stand and I go to bed and I let the radio say Tuesday again and I let it say it and I don't fight it. The couch is in Pittsburgh. My sister has the van. The hallway is a hallway. I will walk it Wednesday. Tonight I am a man on a bench in an empty depot and that is the whole of the evening and I do not need it to mean more than that.
decision.intention: Pittsburgh was already done. I boarded the coach. I rode it. I called. I said the time and the hallway and the noon deadline. I woke up in the bed with the radio saying Tuesday. So the destination is not the act. The act is sitting still. The act is not picking up the phone, not walking to the piano, not walking to the Rialto, not walking to the party. The act is staying where I am, on this bench, in this empty room, with the diesel smell and the cold iron and the red light on the open line that I will not touch. The couch moves Wednesday. My sister is at her place. The van is booked. I will be there by noon. That is the practical thing. The rest of tonight is mine and I will spend it sitting still on a bench in a depot that is not on the broadcast, not on the screen, not in the ballroom, not in the Rialto. Just the bench. Just the count. Just the body in the cold.
decision.words: —(I sit. I count. I do not speak. The line hums. The tracks are black. I stay.)—-
